summary: An Indologist and linguist, Richard Pischel earned his doctorate under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and completed his habilitation at the University of Breslau, also studying under Albrecht Weber. He held professorships at Kiel, Halle-Wittenberg (1885-1902), and Berlin (1902-1908).

Richard Polenberg was an American history scholar who studied at Brooklyn College and Columbia University. He served as a Professor of American History at Cornell University from 1966 to 2011 and was a Fulbright Visiting Professor at Hebrew University.

Philosopher Richard Rorty studied at the University of Chicago and Yale University. He held professorships at Princeton University (1962-1982), the University of Virginia (1982-1998), and Stanford University (appointed 1998), along with visiting posts at UCL, Cambridge, and Harvard.

Richard S. Cohen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Walter M. Spink and Luis Oscar Gómez. He serves as Associate Professor of South Asian Religious Literatures at the University of California, San Diego.

Specializing in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, Richard Salomon studied under Ludo Rocher. He held a professorship at the University of Washington (attested 1998-2017) and was a foreign visiting researcher at Soka University in 2007.

Richard Schechner studied at Cornell University, the University of Iowa, and Tulane University. Beginning around 1967, he served as a University Professor at the Tisch School of the Arts at New York University.

Indologist Richard Schmidt completed his doctorate under Richard Pischel and Karl Friedrich Geldner and habilitated at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg. He worked as a DMG librarian (1904-1910) and became an ordinary professor at the University of Münster in 1910.
Active in linguistics and history, Richard Shilleto was educated at Repton School, Shrewsbury School, and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1828-1832).

Scholar of philosophy and Indology Richard Sorabji was educated at Charterhouse School, Dragon School, and Pembroke College. He served on the faculties of Cornell University (~1962-1970), King's College London (~1970-2000), and Gresham College (~2000-2006).

Linguist Richard Sproat studied at UC San Diego and MIT. He served on the faculties of the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (2003-2009) and Oregon Health and Science University (2009-2012) before joining Google in 2012.

Philosopher Richard Sylvan studied at Victoria University of Wellington and Princeton University. His career included appointments at the University of Sydney (~1963-1966) and as a fellow at the Australian National University in 1971.

Working in history, Central Asian, and Buddhist studies, Richard Taupier earned his doctorate and MS at the University of Massachusetts Amherst, where he became Associate Director of Research Development. He also served as a Visiting Lecturer at Smith College.

Indologist Richard W. Lariviere studied at the University of Iowa and earned his doctorate at the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher. He held administrative posts at UT Austin, the University of Kansas, the University of Oregon, and the Field Museum.

Sinologist Richard Wilhelm studied at Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium and the University of Tübingen. He was a visiting professor at Peking University in 1923 and held the chair of Sinology at Goethe University Frankfurt from 1924, founding the university in 1925.

Indologist and philosopher Richard von Garbe studied at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth and completed his habilitation at Königsberg. He was an extraordinarius at Königsberg (1878-1894) before succeeding Roth as chair at the University of Tübingen (1895-1927).
Historian and sinologist Richard von Glahn became a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles around 1987 and served as a visiting fellow at the University of Tokyo from 1988 to 1989.
Rigdzin Shikpo was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied under teachers Chögyam Trungpa and Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche.
Rigzin Lhundup was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, attested in 1959 and 1987.

Riika J. Virtanen is a Tibetologist who completed doctoral studies at the University of Helsinki under supervisors Asko Parpola, Klaus Karttunen, and Hannu Riikonen, having also studied under teacher Sangye Tandar Naga.
Scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology Rikizan Ishikawa studied at Komazawa University from ~1963 to 1974 and served as Professor of Buddhist Studies there until 1997.
